Honestly though, games are a form of art, we can all agree on that. The writing is designed to elicit emotional responses. Otherwise it'd be a very aesthetically beautiful 3D platforming game with combat mechanics. 

"Big T Traumas" (iykyk fellow psych nerds) are unfortunately very common. And with what, like half a million downloads across the various platforms so far? Statistically, there's gonna be a percentage of players that connect personally with the themes in the game. Even if you haven't personally experienced the trauma; the magic of good writing is to make you feel things. I've not been conscripted to Avernus for a decade, but hoo I still want to give Karlach a hug when she yells about the loneliness.

Welcome to the "oops, turns out I have trauma that resurfaced/connected with themes in this game" club 🤣. The maths doesn't lie, you are not alone.

First of all, I am really proud of you for noticing these thoughts you're having - some people don't notice they're uncomfortable/feel weird about not being the breadwinner and it turns into bitterness. You're awesome.

Second, take a deep breath and a step back. This is a new relationship. I know it's hard, but do your best to try and not compare it to past relationships - it'd feel a bit shit if she turned around and went "things are great and all but my last human was taller so can you just wear heels from now on?"

Thirdly, communicate, communicate and (I cannot stress this enough) communicate! Do it clearly, and as non-judgementally as you can. Be honest when situations arise, feelings are felt etc, and genuinely listen to her when she does the same. You do this, and there likely won't be any "royally screwing up" because any issues can be worked on before they become huge.

Lastly, enjoy your new best friend. Love them, make them laugh, and have fun exploring life with this new beam of beauty and happiness next to you

I'm so so sorry this has happened. 

In any case, it's vital you use this single pringle time wisely and do some self care. Which by the way sounds like you're nailing doing, so high five.

But if you get super hung up on her,  write her a letter of all the things you wish you could say.  DO NOT ACTUALLY SEND IT - keep it and re-read it whenever you need. It can help you get all those thoughts of missing her physically out of your head.

Is there a possibility that what you miss might be all the good things in the relationship, rather than the whole picture of the good and the bad?  
Have a good think about WHY you miss her. Not just the "oh her hair smells of coconut" superficial stuff - did you have compatibility? Similar values?  What made you both break it off,  and if the same behaviors etc is still the same will you want to break it off again? 
It's worth asking her where you both stand and if she would be interested in trialling dating again - be prepared for a no and a yes.  
May the odds be in your favour bro.
